FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE 
May 27, 2014 
CONTACT: City Councilor Brad Winter, 505-489-0327 
 
 
City Councilor Isaac Benton, 505-553-5675 
 
 
County Commissioner Maggie Hart Stebbins, 505-503-0314 
 
 
County Commissioner Wayne Johnson, 505-238-9352 
 
 
NM Senator Bill O’Neill, 505-450-9263 
 
 
NM Senator Sander Rue, 505-301-0189 
 
 
City, County, State and UNMH Partner in Addressing Mental Health,  
Substance Abuse and Homelessness in Albuquerque 
 
ALBUQUERQUE – A bipartisan group of elected officials representing the City of 
Albuquerque, Bernalillo County and the State of New Mexico announced today a collaborative 
effort to address the issues of homelessness, mental health, and substance abuse in Albuquerque.  
A Working Group and a Task Force will be formed to make recommendations to policy makers 
about coordination, resource needs and programs.  
 
The group met last week, along with representatives with subject matter expertise from each 
entity and UNMH, to identify members of a small, core Working Group and to establish a 
process for identifying members of a larger advisory Task Force. They also outlined 
responsibilities of each group. 
 
The Working Group will consist of a representative from the City, County, State, UNMH, 
District Court and Metro Court. Funding for a paid coordinator was included in the budget 
recently passed by City Council for the upcoming fiscal year beginning in July.  This group will 
take input from the Task Force. 
 
The Task Force will include a variety of stakeholder representatives, including the elected 
officials, consumers, service providers, funders, insurers, advocates, crises response and 
corrections. A webpage on the City of Albuquerque website has been set up at

The Council of the 
City of Albuquerque 
 
May 5th, 2014 
 
WHEREAS, the NCAA Division I Indoor Track and Field Championships were held in Albuquerque, 
New Mexico on March 14th and 15th, 2014 at the Albuquerque Convention Center; and 
 
WHEREAS, through the collaborative partnership between the City of Albuquerque Parks and 
Recreation Department, the Albuquerque Convention Center, the University of New Mexico Athletics 
Department and the Albuquerque Convention and Visitors Bureau, this event was a huge success; and 
 
WHEREAS, hosting this prestigious national championship brings positive attention to the City of 
Albuquerque and showcases its best assets, creating potential for more visitors in the future; and   
 
WHEREAS, the University of New Mexico Athletics Department secured the bid to host the 2014 
NCAA Men’s and Women’s Indoor Track and Field Division I National Championships; and 
 
WHEREAS, ACVB reports that this event brought 1,600 attendees and 3,018 room nights generating $1 
million in direct spending; and 
 
WHEREAS, the Albuquerque Convention Center accommodated over 520 athletes from 134 different 
schools during the NCAA Division I Indoor Track and Field Championships; and 
 
WHEREAS, the City of Albuquerque Parks and Recreation Department has maintained and supported 
the indoor track for a period of 9 years and continued to keep it in the professional condition necessary 
to host a national championship. 
 
BE IT PROCLAIMED THAT THE COUNCIL, THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF 
ALBUQUERQUE, HEREBY RECOGNIZES 
 
THE NCAA DIVISION I INDOOR TRACK AND FIELD CHAMPIONSHIPS

The Council of the 
City of Albuquerque 
 
December 2, 2013 
 
WHEREAS, Commander Bonnie Montoya received her Bachelor’s degree from UNM and began her 
distinguished career with the Albuquerque Police Department in 1993 working in Field Services and 
Criminal Investigations; and 
 
WHEREAS, In 2000 Commander Bonnie Montoya was promoted to Sergeant and oversaw the Criminal 
Investigations division which included robbery, violent crimes, homicide, domestic violence, sex crimes, 
missing persons and spent time working on Operations Review under Chief Galvin; and 
 
WHEREAS, Commander Montoya was promoted to Lieutenant in 2006 and graduated from the National 
FBI Academy in 2009 while simultaneously completing her Master’s at UNM; and  
 
WHEREAS, Commander Montoya’s career included over 30 on-site officer-involved shooting 
investigations and over 500 violent crimes scenes; and  
 
WHEREAS, Commander Montoya has served on hundreds of high profile cases including that of the 118th 
Street murders, the baby Angel case, the Ellen Roth Murder, the Ether Man rape investigation and helped 
in solving the long-standing cold case of Michael Snyder; and  
 
WHEREAS, Bonnie Montoya was promoted to Commander in 2011 overseeing the North East Area 
Command, the largest of the six area commands; and  
 
WHEREAS, Commander Montoya’s experience with the Family Advocacy Center and Criminal 
Investigations lead her to champion the need for kid’s ID kits, allowing parents to have their children’s 
finger prints recorded to aid police recovery in the event those children are ever stolen or lost; and  
 
WHEREAS, Commander Montoya has received countless awards from Neighborhood Associations 
commending her dedication to making the Albuquerque community a safer place to live; and 
 
 
BE IT PROCLAIMED THAT THE COUNCIL, THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF 
ALBUQUERQUE, HEREBY RECOGNIZES THE COMMITMENT OF COMMANDER BONNIE 
MONTOYA FOR PROTECTING AND SERVING THE CITIZENS OF ALBUQUERQUE

saved_evidence.title: North Domingo Baca Park Master Development Plan, February 3, 2005
saved_evidence.description: The City's master development plan for the 32-acre North Domingo Baca Park sets the park program, site layout, architectural and landscape design standards, grading and drainage analysis, budget, phasing, and the review path each future facility must follow.
saved_evidence.evidence: Born-digital PDF with a full text layer, 44 pages. Titled North Domingo Baca Park MASTER DEVELOPMENT PLAN, City of Albuquerque Department of Municipal Development, February 3, 2005. The park is bounded by Wyoming Boulevard, Carmel Avenue, Louisiana Boulevard and Corona Avenue, with an adjacent 27-acre AMAFCA property available for joint use. Eight sections plus a general plant list appendix: executive summary, site analysis, community issues, master plan, design standards, grading and drainage, project budget, and phasing.
saved_evidence.why_retained: It is regulatory, not descriptive. Section 8 sets the future review and approval process: the Multi-Generational Center, Library and Pool Complex must be reviewed and approved by the Environmental Planning Commission, while all other park features proceed directly to the Design Review Committee for a work order. It also fixes design standards for architecture, setbacks, building height, parking, lighting, signage, walls and fences, site furniture, landscape, irrigation and utilities, and it carries a conceptual grading and drainage report with peak-discharge calculations against Kinney Dam. Nothing of this kind for this park is held anywhere in the archive.

cross_listings.reason: It is a master development plan whose major elements are subject to Environmental Planning Commission approval, which is the class of record that page carries.
That page already schedules North Domingo Baca Park work in three separate bond records without holding the plan those projects build out.

saved_evidence.already_archived_check: Searched the inventory and the R2 inventory for North Domingo Baca objects. The archive holds nothing for this park: the only Domingo Baca object in R2 is the Paseo del Norte and South Domingo Baca Trail Guide, a different place. North Domingo Baca Park Master Development Plan
21
MASTER PLAN DRAINAGE REPORT
INTRODUCTION
The North Domingo Baca Park is located in 
the Northeast Heights of Albuquerque.  It is 
bounded on the north by Corona Avenue, on 
the east by Wyoming Boulevard, on the south by 
Carmel Avenue and on the west by the Kinney 
Dam and Louisiana Boulevard.  The total park 
area is approximately 38 acres.  The Park loca-
tion is indicated on Figure 1, Location Map.
According to the City of Albuquerque (COA) 
Development Process Manual (DPM), Sec-
tion 22.2, Hydrology, Figure A-1, the project 
is located entirely within Precipitation Zone 3. 
The design storm is the 100-year, 6 hour storm 
event.  The Peak Discharge per acre is found in 
Table A-9 of Section 22.2.  The runoff volume is 
estimated using the excess precipitation found 
in Table A-8.
This drainage report investigates the design 
storm peak runoff rates and volumes for three 
conditions:
• 
the existing conditions
• 
Phase 1 development conditions
• 
full development conditions.
EXISTING CONDITIONS
The western 25 percent of the parcel is taken up 
by the Kinney Dam, which is owned by AMAF-
CA.  This portion of the parcel is not included 
in the drainage analysis.  The existing conditions 
drainage basins are shown on Sheet 1 of 3, which 
is included at the end of this report.
SECTION 6
GRADING AND DRAINAGE
The remaining 75 percent of the parcel is native 
soils and vegetation with some manmade distur-
bance.  However, the observed existing man-
made disturbances are not significant enough to 
affect the Land Treatment type. Therefore, the 
entire parcel under consideration is classified 
as Land Treatment A for the existing conditions 
computations.
The existing site is divided into three sub-basins. 
Basin X1 is the southern portion of the parcel 
and it drains directly into the dam’s pool partially 
by sheet flow and partially by shallow concen-

saved_evidence.but_see: It is a usable lead sheet. It reports that the Council had recently passed the Neighborhood Traffic Management Plan adopting new traffic-calming policy guidelines and treatments, with an amendment requiring the Department of Municipal Development to report back on the criteria in two years, and that the 2015 general obligation bonds designate $1 million for design and analysis of an indoor pool at North Domingo Baca Park. Neither the NTMP nor that report-back is held.

Councilors Corner- March 2015 Edition 
 
Councilor’s Corner –Vice President, Brad Winter 
 
  
 
 
 
Happy March! This is our inaugural edition of the bi-monthly Councilor’s 
Corner update. I encourage you to include this in your neighborhood association 
mailer, pamphlet, or on-line webpage. The Councilor’s corner is about the 
important work we are doing within district 4. (Please see the district’s 
boundaries in the map to the right).  
 
Our Department of Municipal Development (DMD) which 
oversees streets and infrastructure has been quite active within district 4.  We 
recently installed traffic lights at Barstow and Carmel. This will help alleviate the 
congestion within this intersection. In another effort to increase safety in our 
community DMD will install speed signs on Jefferson. In mid-March the speed 
signs will be placed both North and South between Osuna and Paseo Del Norte. In 
the meantime, we are working with the Valley Area Command to have increased 
patrols by the Albuquerque Police Department (A.P.D) throughout the Jefferson 
corridor. We are also working to improve pedestrian safety, walkability and 
beautification along Wyoming. Thanks to the help of our Parks and Recreation 
department you will soon see landscaped medians on Wyoming from Carmel to 
Oakland this will not only enhance the aesthetics of this area but will also help to 
deter mid-block pedestrian crossings. Please, for your safety, use the designated 
cross walks! Also occurring on Wyoming between Alameda and Modesto we will 
be installing curb, gutter, sidewalk and a wheel-chair accessible ramp.  
The City Council recently passed the Neighborhood Traffic Management 
Plan (NTMP) which adopts a new set of policy guidelines and treatments for 
traffic calming in the City of Albuquerque. I voted to remove an Average Daily 
Traffic threshold for speed humps in response to concerns that it was too high.

The Council of the 
City of Albuquerque 
February 25, 2013 
 
WHEREAS, the vision of the Boy Scouts of America is to prepare every  youth in America to become 
responsible, participating citizens and leaders, who are guided by the Scout Oath and Law; and 
 
WHEREAS, Mark Shover, a student at Desert Ridge Middle School, and a member of Boy Scout Troop 
220, has completed the requirements, and was examined by the Eagle Scout Board of Review which 
found him worthy of the rank of Eagle Scout December 20, 2012, the highest rank in the Boy Scouts of 
America; and 
 
WHEREAS, the Boy Scouts of America encourage Eagle Scout candidates to complete worthy projects 
to improve their neighborhoods, their community and the region; and  
 
WHEREAS, Mark’s Eagle project included the restoration of the ball field bleachers and horseshoe pits 
at Elks Refuge in the Sandia Mountains. This project included raising funds to purchase required 
building materials, building the horseshoe pit boxes and benches. The restoration of the ball field 
bleachers also included water proofing, terracing the ground and adding wood chips around the 
bleachers. The horseshoe pits were all newly constructed boxes which were installed on a fully restored 
site; and 
 
WHEREAS, Mark is also a talented musician and a member of the Desert Ridge Middle School Concert 
and Jazz Band I as first chair alto saxophonist and the New Mexico Jazz Workshop Middle School 
Honors Jazz Band as first chair tenor saxophonist; and 
 
WHEREAS, Mark Shover serves as an example to youth through his high level of personal achievement, 
leadership and community service and has made the City of Albuquerque and State of New Mexico very 
proud. 
 
 
BE IT PROCLAIMED THAT THE COUNCIL, THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF 
ALBUQUERQUE, HEREBY RECOGNIZES  
 
EAGLE SCOUT MARK SHOVER 
 
 
 
 
Ken Sanchez, Vice President 
District 1 
 
 
Roxanna Meyers 
District 2 
 
 
Isaac Benton 
District 3 
 
 
Brad Winter 
District 4

City of Albuquerque 
 
April 19th, 2014 
 
WHEREAS, the City of Albuquerque welcomes a delegation from the Kenyan Consulate based in Los 
Angeles led by the Consul General, Ambassador Dr. Wenwa A. Oranga; and 
 
WHEREAS, the delegation including the trade attaché, among others, are in Albuquerque to participate 
in Kenya’s Golden Jubilee, their 50 year celebration of independence from Great Britain; and 
 
WHEREAS, the Kenyan-American community in Albuquerque and throughout New Mexico is hosting a 
luncheon to commemorate the occasion; and 
 
WHEREAS, the luncheon will also serve as an opportunity to conduct a ‘meet-and-confer’ session on 
trade, investment and the recent discovery of oil and other issues of interest to the Kenyan-Americans in 
Albuquerque, New Mexico. 
 
 
BE IT PROCLAIMED THAT THE COUNCIL, THE GOVERNING BODY OF THE CITY OF 
ALBUQUERQUE, HEREBY RECOGNIZES 
 
 
 
A DELEGATION FROM THE KENYAN CONSULATE IN LOS ANGELES THAT IS LED BY 
CONSUL GENERAL, AMBASSADOR DR. WENWA A. ORANGA
